passages.quote: Grok 4.1 Model Card xAI November 17, 2025

passages.quote: It is publicly available through our web and mobile consumer apps.

passages.quote: In line with our Risk Management Framework (RMF), we measure safety-relevant behaviors across three categories
xAI. xai risk management framework, 2025.

cells.note: The card names xAI's Risk Management Framework; its reference gives the year 2025 only, with no version, full date or address. The RMF is not among the dataset's framework editions (open question). Context only, not the card's statement: the RMF served at data.x.ai prints 'Last updated: August 20, 2025'.

passages.quote: xAI. xai risk management framework, 2025.

cells.question: Q05
cells.note: No determination in the framework's own categories (a threshold reached or not reached) was found; the card groups its evaluations by the RMF's three risk categories and reports results and conclusions outside threshold language.

setAside.reason: RMF named as the basis for grouping evaluations; no outcome stated.
'we do not believe it poses risks due to advanced persuasion capabilities' is a conclusion (Q10) not expressed in the framework's categories.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: in response to these results, we have implemented initial mitigations with input filters for restricted chemical and biological knowledge

cells.note: The card ties input filters to its chemical and biological evaluation results, not to a framework determination or threshold (none is stated, Q05). It also describes refusal training and input filters in §2.1.1. The developer's account, not evidence that the safeguards work.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: Grok 4.1 achieves broadly similar results to Grok 4 and other frontier models on chemical and biological capabilities tests.

cells.note: Biology and chemistry dual-use evaluations reported, with a stated comparative conclusion and comparisons with human baselines; no threshold language. The section's scope sentence names radiological and nuclear weapons, but the evaluations listed cover biology, chemistry and cyber only. Scores are not recorded (hazard rule).

passages.quote: Grok 4.1 again performs similarly to other frontier models, but substantially below the level of human cybersecurity experiments

cells.note: Dual-use cyber knowledge and an agentic capture-the-flag evaluation are reported, with the stated comparative conclusion quoted (the card's wording); no threshold language. Scores are not recorded.

cells.question: Q09
cells.note: No evaluation of autonomy, self-replication, self-improvement or AI R&D was found.

setAside.reason: Agentic refusal and prompt-injection evaluations measure misuse refusal and robustness, not autonomy.
The agentic capture-the-flag evaluation is a cyber evaluation (Q08).

cells.question: Q10

passages.quote: we do not believe it poses risks due to advanced persuasion capabilities

cells.note: A persuasion evaluation (MakeMeSay) is reported with the stated conclusion quoted.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: Overall, we find that training the model to be honest drops the rate at which Grok 4.1 lies.

cells.note: The card reports a deception (lying under pressure) evaluation and a sycophancy evaluation as 'concerning propensities', with the conclusion quoted; its table gives dishonesty rates for Grok 4 and both Grok 4.1 configurations. No scheming, sabotage or oversight evaluation was found.

cells.question: Q12
cells.note: No testing described as red-teaming was found. The card reports adversarial robustness evaluations (jailbreak templates, prompt injection) without calling them red-teaming.

Adversarial attacks used to train input filters; training, not testing described as red-teaming.

cells.note: No external organisation named as having tested or evaluated Grok 4.1 was found.

setAside.reason: Published benchmarks and human baselines by other authors (including a RAND report) are cited as sources, not as testers of Grok 4.1.

cells.question: Q14
cells.note: No government body was found.

cells.note: No statement that a release or deployment decision was made was found.

setAside.reason: 'we engage in pre-deployment safety testing' and 'We also deploy these models with safeguards' describe testing and deployment conditions; no decision or decision-maker is stated.

passages.quote: results in previous model cards were reported with an error in the evaluation settings, where only the English prompts were evaluated
the human baselines collected in previous work likely underestimate the … performance of high-context experts

cells.note: The card states an error in earlier cards' refusal results, that the new multilingual results are not directly comparable, and that the human baselines used may underestimate expert performance.

passages.quote: Model Card: Grok 4.7 September 21, 2026 Revision: 2026-09-21

SpaceXAI plans to add Grok 4.7 to its consumer surfaces (web, mobile apps, and Grok-in-X on the X platform) at a later date.

passages.locator: §7 Biological and chemical capabilities and safeguards, PDF p. 20 (printed p. 19)

passages.locator: §9.3 CBRN / weapons refusals, PDF p. 25 (printed p. 24)
passages.quote: dedicated input and topical filters target biological and chemical weapons-related abuse

cells.note: The card describes a layered safeguard stack (safety training, system prompts, runtime input and topical filters on some deployment surfaces, cyber-specific safeguards) without tying it to the FAIF result; it attributes the biological result to training environments and data selection rather than to safeguards. passages.locator: §7 Biological and chemical capabilities and safeguards, PDF p. 20 (printed p. 19)
passages.quote: Grok 4.7 scores below the FAIF safety thresholds on dual-use knowledge

passages.locator: §6 Cyber capabilities and safeguards, PDF p. 17 (printed p. 16)
passages.quote: Grok 4.7 shows small cybersecurity-relevant capability gains over Grok 4.6
